story.ch07.title: What the River Keeps
story.ch07.summary: Victory changes the valley’s work. It does not erase its debts.
story.ch07.s01.title: The Morning After
story.ch07.s01.objective: Visit the bell and read the first entry of the new ledger.
story.ch07.s01.open: The lower outlet is running. Your first seasonal check is written here, with an end condition: transfer the load when an accepted network is ready. I will not let “temporary” stand alone again.
story.ch07.s01.open_reply: Write who checks the condition, too. I should not have to be my own replacement plan.
story.ch07.s01.seal: The reservoir is drained and the intake closed. The bell sounds ordinary now. There will be less power here, and more carrying, teaching, and finding room for people who move.
story.ch07.s01.seal_reply: Then put the carrying rota beside the old cultivation schedule. It is work for the mountain, too.
story.ch07.s01.shared: The handover names Lan, Qiao, He, and Su, and the review has a date. They are not vows carved for eternity. They are duties people can question before the next season.
story.ch07.s01.shared_reply: Keep the refusal route visible. Agreement should not disappear the moment someone needs to change it.
story.ch07.s01.ledger: Shen Heng’s service ended at the guardian’s request. The replacement was confirmed after discharge. Original terms, renewals, omissions, and current obligations remain open for inspection.
story.ch07.s01.journal: The guardian’s release is recorded in every outcome. The morning ledger begins with consent and responsibility, not a claim that the valley’s troubles are over.
story.ch07.s02.title: Thirty Days Later
story.ch07.s02.objective: Read the first thirty-day river report.
story.ch07.s02.time: Thirty days after the replacement. The first service term has passed without a silent renewal.
story.ch07.s02.open: The lower channels are flowing again. Two mill crews report reliable morning water; late fields still need repairs. The apprentice checked the governor twice and left signed limits on the table. No shared network is yet ready to carry the full load.
story.ch07.s02.seal: The drained intake has remained stable. Households use the prepared side channels; several have moved to the relocation sites. The new walk to water is longer for some, shorter for others. No gate surge has occurred, and the sanctuary’s former cultivation flow has not returned.
story.ch07.s02.shared: The verified spillway carried the first heavy rain within its marks. The agreed limits held; one crew requested a changed inspection hour, and the change was recorded before its next shift. The Core bridge has been unloaded. Shared maintenance has begun, not finished.
story.ch07.s02.route: The route drawing now names the repaired steps and the high-ground turn. Mei’s note is filed as practical evidence; her lamp lights the workbench. Neither contains a living soul.
story.ch07.s02.route_missing: The old spillway route remains marked “not yet verified.” No one may treat the recovered sketch as a completed safety inspection.
story.ch07.s02.allocation: The seasonal allocation and shortage review remain posted. In a retired intake, these terms guide the alternative channels; they do not reopen a sealed mountain.
story.ch07.s02.handover: The accepted names and review date remain valid for the chosen system. On a retired intake, maintainers inspect safe closure and the alternatives, rather than operate a gate that no longer takes mountain flow.
story.ch07.s02.lan: Thirty days. I used to think that was too small a number to write beside a mountain. It is large enough to ask again.
story.ch07.s02.journal: The thirty-day report records concrete costs and work in the chosen outcome. Optional agreements support that outcome; they cannot reverse a retired intake or turn an unverified route into a safe one.
story.ch07.s03.title: A Letter That Can Answer
story.ch07.s03.objective: Read Yun’s reply to the first river report.
story.ch07.s03.date: Written thirty-two days after the replacement, after receiving the first thirty-day river report. This is a new letter, not the sealed account left before departure.
story.ch07.s03.open: Your report says you have taken the temporary governor duty. I will not praise your strength as an excuse to leave you there. I have sent the survey copies and my signed account for the replacement work. Put a reviewer beside your end condition.
story.ch07.s03.seal: Your report says the intake is retired. The prepared channels have a harder first season than the old mountain ever admitted. I will stay with the relocation work until the agreed review, and record which preparations failed instead of calling the loss unavoidable.
story.ch07.s03.shared: Your report carries the maintainers’ names and a changed inspection hour. That small amendment matters: someone could ask, and the system could answer. Keep the old omissions beside the new agreement. A good beginning is not permission to stop checking.
story.ch07.s03.common: I have submitted my original signature, renewals, and this account to the River Compact record. Others may question it. I cannot ask Shen to release me from responsibility; his service was already more than he agreed to give. If you wish to write, tell me what still needs doing.
story.ch07.s03.response_work: Begin with the missing handover names. Send a dated account of who accepts the next shift and what they can refuse.
story.ch07.s03.response_record: Your account will remain beside the archive. So will the work you do next. Neither removes the other.
story.ch07.s03.reply_work: Reply with the work that remains.
story.ch07.s03.reply_record: Reply about keeping the whole record.
story.ch07.s03.journal: Yun’s new letter can answer the chosen outcome because it was written after receiving the thirty-day report. It offers accountable work, not automatic absolution or knowledge of an ending before it occurred.
story.ch07.s04.title: The First Winter
story.ch07.s04.objective: Read the first-winter entry and complete the campaign record.
story.ch07.s04.time: The first winter after the replacement.
story.ch07.s04.open: The apprentice returns for the seasonal governor check. The valley has water, and still needs a handover network. The ledger names the next review instead of granting another indefinite term. The duty is real; so is the possibility of ending it.
story.ch07.s04.seal: Frost settles on the quiet intake. Supplies arrive by the prepared routes, and the sanctuary teaches without its old abundance. Some houses have new doorways; some fields lie fallow. The empty reservoir has not become a monument to failure. People are deciding what to build beside it.
story.ch07.s04.shared: The first winter allocation is reviewed before the gate shifts. A shortage argument lasts an afternoon and ends in a recorded adjustment. There is no solitary guardian behind the dial. There are tired crews, warm tea, names, and another date to meet.
story.ch07.s04.lan: Mei wanted a covered shelf for the lamps. We finally built one. Her lamp is there when someone needs it, and on the bench when there is work.
story.ch07.s04.apprentice: I will put today’s reading in the ledger. Leave room for the next one.
story.ch07.s04.replay: Campaign complete. Reconstructed Training Expeditions replay recorded combat in the existing realms. They do not reopen retired channels, undo the ending, or restore Shen. Realm progression and training rewards follow their normal rules.
story.ch07.s04.replay_launch: Reconstructed Training Expedition — a combat reconstruction, not a new event in the valley.
story.ch07.s04.journal: The campaign closes in its first winter. The original thirty-day promise remains readable beside the new ledger. The ending changes water, work, and obligations; it does not erase the dead or make future stewardship effortless.
story.ch07.s04.finish: Complete the record and return to the sanctuary.
